# cloudminator_bucket_key (Resource)

An S3 access key scoped to one bucket. The secret is returned only when the key is created; an imported key has no `secret_access_key`.

~> The secret is stored in the Terraform state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cloudminator_bucket" "backups" {
  name = "acme-backups"
}

resource "cloudminator_bucket_key" "restic" {
  bucket = cloudminator_bucket.backups.id
  name   = "restic"
}

output "access_key_id" {
  value = cloudminator_bucket_key.restic.access_key_id
}

output "secret_access_key" {
  value     = cloudminator_bucket_key.restic.secret_access_key
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `bucket` (String) Bucket name (`cloudminator_bucket.id`).

### Optional

- `name` (String) Key name. Defaults to `<bucket>-key`.
- `org` (String) Organization slug. Defaults to the provider's `org`. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `project` (String) Project slug. Defaults to the provider's `project` (or `default`). Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `access_key_id` (String) S3 access key id.
- `id` (String) The access key id.
- `secret_access_key` (String, Sensitive) S3 secret access key (only known for keys created by Terraform).
- `simulated` (Boolean) True when the platform served this from a simulated (non-production) backend: nothing real exists behind it.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a bucket key by organization, project, bucket and access key id.
# The secret is only returned at creation, so an imported key has no secret_access_key.
terraform import cloudminator_bucket_key.restic acme/default/acme-backups/GK0123456789abcdef
```
